changelog: [When to Segment]: corrected the quotative rule — evidence (E00140) showed cutting between a -다고/-라고 quote and its reporting verb drops the quoted content; the rule now keeps quote+reporting verb in one segment and only permits a cut after the whole reported-speech unit when a distinct matrix clause with its own subject+verb follows.

[When to Segment]: added eight narrow, generalizable permissive rules for measured under-segmentation — coordinating -고 with two independently-complete clauses; causal -아서/-어서/-니까 with an independent result clause; conditional -면/-다면 with an independent consequence clause; comparative -보다는 between two self-standing clauses; chained sequential temporal markers (나중에, 끝나고 나서, etc.) each closing its own time clause; a leading discourse adverb (어쨌든/아무튼/결국) before a full independent clause; an unambiguous short subject pronoun before a long self-contained predicate; a repeated/restated subject immediately before its own predicate. Each rule requires the resulting pieces to be independently complete, to avoid the quality-floor failures seen when broader versions of these rules were tried without that requirement.

[When to Segment]: narrowed the sentence-initial discourse-marker rule to short single-word connectives (그래서, 그런데, 근데, 아니, 그냥, 그니까) — longer multi-word lead-ins (e.g. 'X를 들어서' type phrases) are excluded from standalone segmentation since isolating them produced verb-less fragments in evidence.
